submission.reasoning: On workstation5, user WORKSTATION5\wardog used an interactive high-integrity cmd.exe (proc-690e6c933a) to run sc.exe (proc-f4d3576242). That sc.exe pointed the Fax service binPath at 'powershell.exe -noexit -c "write-host 'T1543.003 Test'"' (MITRE T1543.003, modify a system service for persistence or privilege escalation). The change landed in the Fax service ImagePath registry value (reg-e3a6a6345f, via rel-36594623fc). The same cmd then ran 'sc start Fax' (proc-cd222a569d). That started the hijacked service: PowerShell (proc-7f9f3418e9) ran as NT AUTHORITY\NETWORK SERVICE. About 6 seconds later, 'sc config Fax binPath= fxssvc.exe' (proc-babd722e6c) set the original binary back. The 'T1543.003 Test' marker matches an Atomic Red Team simulation. The behaviour is still a real service hijack that ran code under a service account, so it is treated as malicious.
